title: M. N. Roy: Radical Humanism and Congress

scenes.text: Can a mental revolution liberate humans more than political independence?
scenes.narration: Imagine winning national independence, yet remaining trapped by fear, dogma, and blind superstition. Thinker M. N. Roy argued that true liberation requires a scientific revolution inside your own mind.

scenes.text: Changing a broken phone cover never fixes a corrupted operating system inside.
scenes.narration: Here is a school analogy to make this click. Changing who rules the country without educating citizens is like putting a fancy cover on a phone with a frozen screen.

scenes.heading: Roy's Three Ideational Phases

events.what: Communist revolutionary and debater against Lenin
Joined Congress and critiqued Marxist doctrines
Founded Radical Humanism for human liberation

scenes.narration: Roy went through an extraordinary intellectual journey. He began as a global communist debating Lenin, briefly joined Congress to radicalize it, and finally developed a new worldview called Radical Humanism.

scenes.heading: Marx versus M. N. Roy
scenes.narration: Here is the trick. Roy broke with Karl Marx by arguing that real revolution comes from transforming human thinking, not just changing economic factories, because history advances through social cooperation.

scenes.heading: Pillars of Radical Humanism
items: Freedom: Complete emancipation from fear and superstition
Reason: Materialistic rationality derived from survival
Ethics: Secular social rules grounded in human reason
scenes.narration: Radical Humanism places the individual human being at the center. Roy taught that reason is born from our struggle for survival, providing a secular foundation for ethics and absolute personal freedom.

scenes.heading: Democratic Power Structure
scenes.narration: Roy rejected parliamentary elections because party bosses hijack power. Instead, he advocated grassroots radical democracy and popular industrial ownership, sharing Gandhi's deep commitment to decentralized, partyless politics.

items: Evolved from revolutionary communism to Radical Humanism
Prioritized mental revolution over material mode of production
Advocated grassroots democracy and secular reason-based ethics
scenes.narration: To recap, remember that Roy evolved beyond communism to Radical Humanism, demanded a mental revolution, and championed grassroots democracy rooted in scientific reason.
